input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Idle and stale resource reports in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers per-project idle resource reporting in the RHOAI web
console so cluster administrators can see which resources are sitting idle
and reclaim capacity with confidence. It adds two report views: an
idle-workbench report showing each workbench's last activity, owner, and
reserved resources, and a stale pipeline-run report showing completed runs
older than a configurable age with their retained artifacts. Both reports
are read-only surfaces over data that already exists in the platform —
notebook-controller activity tracking and Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata —
so this epic changes only the web console; the data-source components keep
working unchanged. Administrators can also export either report as CSV.

## Scope

- Add a per-project idle-workbench report view to the web console showing,
  per workbench: last activity (sourced from the notebook controller's
  activity tracking), owner, and reserved resources.
- Add a per-project stale pipeline-run report view to the console showing
  completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age threshold, with
  their retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Make the stale-run age threshold configurable.
- Add CSV export of either report, containing the columns the report
  displays.
- Validation of the passive data sources: confirm the idle-workbench report
  matches notebook-controller activity data, and the stale-run report
  matches Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata, without changes to either
  data-source component.
- No automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources, and no
  cost/chargeback calculations (out of scope per the strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing recent activity,
  when an administrator opens the idle-workbench report, then every
  workbench in the project is listed with its last-activity timestamp,
  owner, and reserved resources, and the values match the notebook
  controller's activity tracking.
- Given a project containing completed pipeline runs of differing ages with
  retained artifacts, when an administrator opens the stale pipeline-run
  report with a configured age threshold, then exactly the completed runs
  older than that threshold are listed with their completion age and
  retained artifacts, and the values match Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Given the stale pipeline-run report, when an administrator changes the age
  threshold configuration, then the report reflects the new threshold
  without code changes.
- Given either report, when an administrator triggers CSV export, then a CSV
  file is produced containing the report's displayed rows and columns.
- The notebook controller and Kubeflow Pipelines components require no code
  changes for either report to function (verified against a running
  platform).
- Measured by: report correctness verified against the underlying
  notebook-controller activity data and Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata in a
  test project.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner,
  reserved resources) sourced from notebook-controller activity tracking —
  covered by the idle-workbench report scope above.
- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
  configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines
  run metadata — covered by the stale-run report scope above.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): CSV export of either report — bundled into this epic
  because it exports the same report data and renders on the same report
  surfaces this epic builds; a separate epic would build the same surfaces
  twice or force a second pass over them.

## Risks / Notes

- The strategy asserts the notebook-controller last-activity data exists
  and only needs surfacing. If the activity timestamps are not readable
  through an interface the console can consume, a follow-up change in the
  notebook controller (Notebooks component, Workbenches team) may be
  required — escalate if that exposure work turns out to be non-trivial.

# Document the idle/stale resource reports and safe reclamation steps

## Description

This epic delivers user documentation for the idle resource reporting
capability in the RHOAI web console. It explains the two reports — the
per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved
resources) and the stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
configurable age with retained artifacts) — how to read and configure them,
how to export them as CSV, and the safe steps administrators can take to
reclaim capacity based on what the reports show. It is written against the
implemented reports after the console work is complete.

## Scope

Content outline:

- A documentation topic introducing idle resource reporting: what problem
  it solves for cluster administrators and where the reports live in the
  web console.
- A topic explaining the idle-workbench report: what each column (last
  activity, owner, reserved resources) means, where the data comes from
  (notebook-controller activity tracking), and its limitations.
- A topic explaining the stale pipeline-run report: what "stale" means, how
  to configure the age threshold, what retained artifacts are, and where
  the data comes from (Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata).
- A topic covering CSV export of either report.
- A topic on safe reclamation steps: how administrators can act on the
  reports to reclaim capacity with confidence, including appropriate
  cautions (e.g., checking with a workbench owner before acting, retaining
  artifacts that matter). Automated reclamation is out of scope for the
  feature and must not be documented as available.
- Screenshots of the report views and export flow as part of the topics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains both reports, the meaning of each
  reported field, the configurable stale-run age threshold, and CSV export.
- Published documentation describes safe reclamation steps an administrator
  can take based on the reports, and does not describe automated
  reclamation/deletion or cost/chargeback capabilities (out of scope per the
  strategy).
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports
  in the web console and matches the shipped behavior (columns, thresholds,
  export output).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation
  steps — covered by the content outline above.

authoring (new doc topics explaining the reports and safe reclamation steps),

own review cycle. Full decomposition therefore applies.
